subject: Orchid Labs: KMS escrow + audit-log granularity questions
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Oct 2026 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: Orchid Labs - KMS escrow + audit-log granularity questions

Hi team,

Orchid Labs (clinical pilot in EU) just surfaced two asks in the procurement call: a) they want an option for key escrow while we run a short pilot (their legal requires split custody for HIE data), and b) they need per-request audit-log granularity (they want to tie tokens to request IDs in logs for 90 days). They also asked whether we can retain a separate, immutable audit stream for a 12-month retention window if needed.

Can we triage quickly: what combinations of Private (VPC) + BYOK + escrow are supported today, what security/legal blockers we anticipate (HSM policy, export controls, key custody SOPs), and whether per-request log granularity is feasible with current ingest and retention pipelines without breaking PII minimization obligations?

Quick asks: 
- Marcus: feasibility/ops impact for escrow + split custody (HSM flow) and estimated lead time.
- Kimberly: compliance e2e—what evidence we can provide (SOC2 controls mapping, KMS key rotation logs, HSM audit statements).
- Jonas/Grace: product constraints for immutable audit streams and per-request indexing (index size, query performance, costs).

I attached the procurement note from Orchid and their one-page legal summary. I'll schedule a 30-min sync after we have initial take.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Director, Customer Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Attachments: requested_evidence_checklist.xlsx (procurement checklist)
From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Oct 2026 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Orchid Labs - KMS escrow + audit-log granularity questions

Vanessa — quick run at answers below. High level first: escrow is operationally doable but will need a narrow, documented process and a short-term exception to our default customer-managed key posture. Key points:

1) Escrow model options (pros/cons)
- Split custody via dual-HSM escrow (customer + Redwood-held escrow): doable. Requires legal to sign off on custody SLA and a tech runbook.
- Time-limited escrow containers (30/90 days) with automatic deletion/confirmation flows: implementable but needs orchestration and audit steps.

2) HSM & KMS impacts
- We'll need an HSM-backed envelope key and an escrow HSM account. Ops will need a small runbook + RBAC update. Expect ~4-6 weeks engineering + 2 weeks ops SOP and runbook.

3) Audit log per-request granularity
- Current audit stream records request metadata and model id; we do not persist full per-token traces. Adding a request_id (GUID) into the existing stream is lightweight.
- Immutable, separate 12-month stream: storage + indexing cost will be material; estimate +18-25% storage costs and an extra ingest pipeline shard. Also need legal review for retention of potentially re-identifying data.

Open items / blockers
- Legal: escrow custody agreement and data residency implications for EU clinical data.
- Product: confirm if Orchid needs decrypted payloads or just proof-of-use (we prefer not to hold plaintext).

I'll follow up with a short tech note and a proposed milestone plan.

—Marcus
Principal Infrastructure Engineer

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Oct 2026 11:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Orchid Labs - KMS escrow + audit-log granularity questions

Thanks Marcus — a few compliance notes:

- Evidence set: we can provide KMS rotation logs, HSM access audit logs (ops actions), SOC2 control mappings, and a canonical escrow runbook template. I've attached the redwood_byo_playbook_v2.pdf snippet that covers escrow examples.
- For EU clinical data, Orchid's DPA will need explicit clauses on key custodianship and incident notification. Recommend we ask legal to draft an exhibit rather than ad-hoc email confirmations.
- Retention window: 12 months for an immutable stream is acceptable from a controls perspective, but we must provide a data minimization statement and a redaction approach (we should strip user-provided identifiers unless explicitly consented).

I'll coordinate with Legal and summarize required contract language.

-Kimberly
Senior Compliance Manager, Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood_byo_playbook_v2.pdf (excerpt on escrow)
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
To: Nina Patel <nina@orchidlabs.com>, Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@orchidlabs.com>, Orchid Labs Legal <legal@orchidlabs.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Oct 2026 09:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Orchid Labs - KMS escrow + audit-log granularity questions

Hi Nina / Tom — thanks for the call today and for outlining the constraints. To summarize our current position and next steps: 

1) Escrow: Redwood can support a time-limited escrow arrangement using a dual-HSM model (customer + Redwood escrow). We will not hold plaintext by default; escrow will be an encrypted envelope key that requires both parties to reconstruct. We need your legal team to confirm acceptable custody language; Kimberly will coordinate contract language.

2) Audit logs: We can add a per-request request_id field to the audit stream and provision an immutable, separate stream for 12-month retention. This will increase storage and query costs — Marcus will provide a cost delta and timeline.

3) Actions & timeline:
- Orchid: confirm whether you require decrypted payloads in escrow or only sealed evidence. (Action: Nina)
- Redwood: Marcus to provide engineering lead time and cost delta by EOD Thu (Action: Marcus).
- Redwood: Kimberly to draft an exhibit for the DPA and proposed redaction language by end of week (Action: Kimberly).

We attached the checklist and a proposed diagram of the escrow flow for your review. Happy to hop on a follow-up 30-min session once we have the answers above.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Director, Customer Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Attachments: orchid_kms_diagram.pdf; requested_evidence_checklist.xlsx
From: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@orchidlabs.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>, Nina Patel <nina@orchidlabs.com>, Orchid Labs Legal <legal@orchidlabs.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Oct 2026 16:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Orchid Labs - KMS escrow + audit-log granularity questions

Vanessa / team — thanks for the clear recap. Quick answers: 

- We do NOT want Redwood to hold decrypted payloads. The escrow is for emergency recovery and must require dual keys (Orchid + Redwood).
- Per-request IDs are fine; we will accept pseudonymized request identifiers if that helps with privacy.
- Legal will work with Kimberly on the exhibit; expect comments by Friday.

Nina will coordinate a follow-up call after you share the cost/delivery estimate.

Regards,
Tom Reynolds
Head of InfoSec, Orchid Labs
